title: developer-consumption-scenarios-catalog-2026
author: Marina Ortega
body:
Title: Developer Consumption Scenarios Catalog (2026)

Purpose:
This catalog describes common developer integration patterns for Redwood Inference, recommended defaults, performance expectations, pricing implications, and product requirements that the product and engineering teams should support. It is intended to guide SDK documentation, onboarding templates, and cost/latency calculators in the Console and Optimize product.

Audience:
- Product managers and technical writers building onboarding flows
- Solutions engineers and SEs onboarding new customers
- SDK and runtime engineers implementing defaults and telemetry
- Sales engineers advising customers on SLA and pricing choices

Executive summary:
We observed five consistent consumption archetypes across customers during Q4 2025 and H1 2026: transactional chat, bulk/async summarization, embedding-heavy search, high-throughput reranking, and multimodal enrichment pipelines. Each archetype has distinct latency SLOs, cost sensitivity, and recommended serving configuration. Supporting clear first-class paths for each will reduce time-to-first-success and lower surprise bills.

Catalog of scenarios (high-level):
1) Transactional chat (conversational UI)
   - Description: Low-latency request/response flows where each request should return a coherent multi-turn response in <200ms P95 for simple prompts and <600ms for long-context turns. Typical for in-app assistants, chatbots, and support UIs.
   - Recommended model variants: conversational-1-small (dev), conversational-1 (default), conversational-1-fp16 (low-latency).
   - SLOs & KPIs: P95 latency target 150–600ms depending on fidelity; error rate <0.5%; context length up to 4k tokens.
   - Default runtime config: streaming enabled, continuous KV caching per session (TTL 30m), batch-size target 8, max-batch-wait 8ms.
   - Cost sensitivity: medium. Recommend dynamic quantization for dev/test; for production prefer fp16 on Dedicated.
   - Pricing guidance: favor per-token pricing with optional concurrency-based discounts for high-throughput chat channels.

2) Bulk/async summarization (document pipelines)
   - Description: Large documents or corpora processed asynchronously. Latency tolerance measured in minutes rather than milliseconds; cost per unit is primary metric.
   - Recommended model variants: summarization-1-medium, summarization-1-quantized-8bit.
   - SLOs & KPIs: throughput (docs/hour), cost per doc, end-to-end latency 1–30 minutes depending on pipeline batching.
   - Default runtime config: large-batch worker pools, aggressive batching (batch-size 64–256), prefix caching disabled across unrelated requests, prefer quantized variants.
   - Cost sensitivity: high — recommend Schedule Jobs + Dedicated Reserved capacity with burst credits.
   - Pricing guidance: use token-bundle discounts and reserved-capacity packages; suggest customers use Redis pre-chunking to reduce token count.

3) Embedding generation at scale (search & vector DB population)
   - Description: Massive embedding workloads for indexing, similarity search, and vector database ingestion. IO-bound and typically offline or streaming.
   - Recommended model variants: embeddings-2-highthroughput, embeddings-2-quantized.
   - SLOs & KPIs: embeddings/sec, token efficiency, batching efficiency. Aim for >10k embeddings/hour per GPU worker for medium-size vectors.
   - Default runtime config: streaming-batch worker with per-request batching window 100–250ms, compacted batching to match vectorizer memory constraints.
   - Cost sensitivity: very high — customers should use Optimize recommendations to enable mixed-precision and larger batch sizes.
   - Pricing guidance: meter by 1) per-embedding unit with tiered volume discounts, or 2) per-job credits for offline cron jobs.

4) Reranking / kNN re-ranker (low-latency re-score)
   - Description: Small inputs with compute-heavy scoring (e.g., scoring 100 candidates). Requires stable latency and predictable cost.
   - Recommended model variants: reranker-1-small (fast), reranker-1 (balanced).
   - SLOs & KPIs: P95 latency <250ms for up to 100 candidates; per-request cost per 100 candidates target.
   - Default runtime config: vectorized scoring kernels, dedicated CPU offload for lightweight prefiltering, batch-size 1 with internal micro-batching for candidates.
   - Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Encourage model distillation or candidate pruning upstream.
   - Pricing guidance: recommend a per-request pricing add-on for high-candidate re-rank workloads or a candidate-count multiplier in billing.

5) Multimodal enrichment pipelines (OCR + LLM + embeddings)
   - Description: Pipelines combining document OCR, image embeddings, and LLM enrichment. These are compositional and often cross service boundaries.
   - Recommended model variants: multimodal-lite (edge), multimodal-core (cloud).
   - SLOs & KPIs: end-to-end pipeline latency; component reliability; per-document cost.
   - Default runtime config: orchestration via Redwood Conductor patterns, per-stage SLOs, and fallback to lower-fidelity model variants.
   - Cost sensitivity: mixed. Visual pre-processing is often dominant cost.
   - Pricing guidance: bundle consumption across stages into a single per-document credit to simplify billing and reduce surprise.

Per-scenario recommended defaults (table):
- Table represented as plain text for Confluence import. Columns: Scenario | Default Model | Batch Strategy | Cache | Typical P95 Latency | Recommended Billing Mode
- Row 1: Transactional chat | conversational-1 | small continuous batching (8) | session KV cache (30m) | 150–600ms | per-token + concurrency discount
- Row 2: Bulk summarization | summarization-1-quant | large batches (64–256) | none | minutes | reserved capacity / token bundles
- Row 3: Embeddings | embeddings-2-qtz | medium batch (50) | no | seconds to minutes | per-embedding unit (volume tiers)
- Row 4: Reranking | reranker-1 | micro-batching internally | ephemeral | <250ms | per-request candidate multiplier
- Row 5: Multimodal | multimodal-core | stage-oriented batching | stage caches | variable | bundled per-document credit

Implementation notes for SDKs and Console:
- SDK defaults: expose a scenario preset parameter (e.g., scenario="chat-transactional") that applies recommended model, max_tokens, KV cache TTL, and batching hints.
- Console: add a Consumption Scenario Selector in onboarding with example throughput, estimated cost per 1k requests, and a toggle for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Optimize: ensure Optimize suggests quantization profiles per scenario and shows estimated cost savings and fidelity delta.

Product requirements (high-level PRD bullets):
1. Scenario presets in SDKs and Console (MVP): provide 5 presets mapped to runtime configs and telemetry tags.
2. Billing meter updates: support candidate-count multiplier for reranking and a per-document bundled credit for multimodal pipelines.
3. Telemetry: add scenario tags to all traces, token meters, and cost attribution so Console can show per-scenario costs.
4. Onboarding templates: produce quickstart repos for each scenario with sample data, infra Terraform for Dedicated testing, and a Q/A checklist.

Operational playbook (onboarding sequence):
1) Customer selects scenario in Console or via SE flow.
2) Console pre-populates recommended model and capacity; shows simulated cost for 1k requests/day.
3) Customer runs sample traffic generator (included in quickstart) for 24h in staging.
4) Solutions engineer reviews telemetry: P95 latency, batching efficiency, token ratio.
5) If cost > expectation, enable Optimize recommendations: quantize, increase batch size, or enable fallback variants.
6) After acceptance, transition to Dedicated (optional) with reserved capacity sizing guide.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- UX simplicity vs configuration granularity: presets must be opinionated but not block advanced users.
- Pricing complexity vs fairness: bundling simplifies bills but must remain transparent for high-volume users.
- Default SLOs must be conservative so early adopters don't observe large regressions.

Roadmap & next steps (quarterly milestones):
- Q1 2026: Launch SDK scenario presets + Console selector (MVP).
- Q2 2026: Telemetry tagging by scenario, consumption cost breakdown in Console.
- Q3 2026: Billing primitives for candidate multipliers and per-document credits.
- Q4 2026: Optimize integration that recommends scenario-specific quantization profiles and simulates fidelity impact.

Signals to measure success:
- Time-to-first-success: median time from signup to serving first 1k requests with stable SLOs (target <72 hours).
- Per-scenario cost accuracy: discrepancy between estimated and actual cost for first 30d (target <15%).
- Onboarding churn: percentage of customers that abandon after staging (target <10%).

Release notes snapshot (v0.1 - published 2026-01-15):
- Introduced Developer Consumption Scenarios Catalog and SDK scenario presets for chat, summarization, embeddings, reranking, and multimodal pipelines.
- Console: added onboarding selector that simulates cost and pre-configures runtime defaults.
- Telemetry: initial scenario tagging implemented for hosted API.

Appendix: Example CLI snippet (chat transactional preset)
$ redwood-cli create-inference-job --scenario chat-transactional --model conversational-1 --concurrency 20 --kv-cache-ttl 1800

JSON example (preset manifest)
{
  "preset": "chat-transactional",
  "model": "conversational-1",
  "batch_target": "8",
  "kv_cache_ttl_seconds": "1800"
}

If you have questions or want this catalog expanded to include industry vertical patterns (healthcare, finance, regulated), open a PR to this page and tag the product owner.
